summary: POST /api/schedules resolves created_by via a second, non-atomic resolve_session_fn call independent of the Write/Execute gates. On nullopt, created_by silently stays '' (schema default) instead of failing closed. Since delete/enable are owner-scoped (WHERE created_by=$N) and '' never matches a real username, the schedule becomes permanently un-deletable/un-disableable via the API. Under RBAC legacy-open (a documented, supported production posture), the orphaned schedule still arms and fires unattended forever, defeating the H-01 kill-switch design intent. Confirmed byte-identical against origin/dev's pre-extraction interim #1806 handle_create_schedule (lines 67-68) - genuinely pre-existing, not introduced by PR-8's mechanical extraction or this merge. Same defect class and same root chokepoint (resolve_session_fn's non-atomic second call) as #4128 (PR-9's Approval API), different consequence.
waiver_rationale: Filed as issue #4131 with full technical detail (both trigger paths, both RBAC-posture consequences, evidence line numbers, acceptance criteria). Documented in-code: schedule_routes.hpp header (KNOWN GAP block) + schedule_routes.cpp's create-route call site (KNOWN GAP comment) + corrected the delete-route's inaccurate 'cannot fail auth' comment to reference #4131 and explain why that route's failure mode is benign. NOT code-fixed in this PR per the established campaign discipline (#3378, #4128 precedent): a verbatim-extraction PR does not silently redesign pre-existing auth-adjacent behavior outside its stated scope; the real remedy (reuse perm_fn's already-validated identity instead of re-resolving) is a design change tracked at #4131, and would also fix #4128's identical pattern.
